Daily Brief

COP31 collapsed without an agreement on Sunday after the European Union formally rejected a final draft text that omitted any explicit reference to fossil fuels [France 24, RFI, The Hindu, Globe and Mail]. The failed summit in Antalya marks a significant setback for international climate diplomacy, with negotiations running more than 40 hours past deadline before breaking down. Meanwhile, tensions in the Baltic escalated as a Russian cargo ship struck by drone attack remained on fire in Finnish waters, with Finnish authorities attributing the strike to Ukraine [BBC, Le Monde]. The Lowy Institute's 2026 Asia Power Index revealed the narrowest power gap between the US and China on record, with Washington's diplomatic influence declining sharply amid its war with Iran [ABC Australia]. In South Korea, Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned following an AI-assisted cheating scandal that disrupted the national college entrance exam [BBC]. Separately, an Indonesian factory fire killed at least three workers with dozens still missing as rescue operations continued [BBC, ABC Australia, France 24].

Top Stories
01 Climate

COP31 Ends in Failure as EU Rejects Climate Deal Lacking Fossil Fuel Reference

  • The European Union formally objected to adopting the final draft text at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, citing the omission of any mention of fossil fuels as unacceptable
  • Negotiations ran more than 44 hours past the official Friday deadline before collapsing, with COP31 President Murat Kurum acknowledging no agreement was reached
  • Panama also formally objected to the proposed deal, joining the EU in blocking consensus among nearly 200 nations
  • The failed text did reference the 2023 Dubai agreement but contained no explicit commitment to phase out coal, oil, or gas

02 Conflict

Russian Cargo Ship Burns in Finnish Waters After Drone Strike Attributed to Ukraine

  • The Sparta II, a sanctioned Russian cargo vessel bound for Kaliningrad, was struck by drones Saturday morning in the Gulf of Finland and drifted into Finnish waters
  • Finnish defence forces stated Ukraine was likely behind the attack; Kyiv has not commented
  • Firefighting and rescue efforts continued Sunday with Finnish, Estonian, and Russian assets involved; the ship had not sunk
  • Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said 'war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity' while affirming Ukraine's right to fight back

US-China Power Gap Narrows to Record Low as Washington Loses Influence in Asia

  • China now ranks first in economic relationships and diplomatic influence measures, ahead of the United States

04 Technology

South Korea Education Minister Resigns Over AI Cheating Scandal That Disrupted National Exam

  • Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned taking responsibility for confusion caused by last-minute anti-cheating measures during the Suneung college entrance exam
  • Emergency alerts were sent to every mobile phone in the country after a top scorer in a tax accountancy exam admitted using AI tools and hidden cameras
  • Officials found 111 candidates with unauthorized smart devices during this year's exam, taken by approximately 500,000 students
  • President Lee Jae Myung, who has called for exam system overhaul, accepted the resignation

Indonesian Factory Fire Kills Three, Leaves Dozens Missing as Rescue Operations Continue

  • A fire broke out at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionary factory in Banten province Saturday evening with approximately 300 workers inside
  • At least three workers confirmed dead with 29 still missing; 24 body bags removed from the factory though each may contain multiple remains
  • The three-story factory was engulfed in flames sending thick black smoke into the sky; firefighters were still tackling some flames Sunday
  • The fire's cause has not yet been determined; rescue operations continue in areas where workers are believed trapped
